content.jointProblem: Can EM38-assisted regression-kriging and uncertainty-guided sampling identify Tisa floodplain salinity pockets of 0.3–0.8 hectares more reliably than TloCare’s four-hectare grid without increasing routine survey costs? A first experiment on representative Tisa fields would test local ECa-to-laboratory salinity calibration and pocket detection using spatially held-out reference samples, comparing the existing grid with sensor-guided sampling while accounting for sensor, fieldwork and laboratory costs.

rationale.text: He has directly relevant experience combining proximal sensing and regression-kriging to map saline-sodic zones on a commercial sunflower farm.

sources.quote: Regression-kriging (RK) was applied to delineate saline-sodic soil management zones at a commercial sunflower farm of 280 hectares in central Vojvodina.
Apparent electrical conductivity (ECa) from an EM38 survey and total sodium content from pXRF scanning served as covariates

rationale.text: His sampling-design research directly addresses the trade-off between laboratory sample count and mapping accuracy, including the failure of overly sparse calibration sets.

sources.quote: this study evaluated the effect of progressively reducing the calibration sample set to 100, 75, 50, 30, and 20 samples
Nugget variance estimates became unstable below n=30, compromising kriging weights.

rationale.text: He has studied the temporal stability of conductivity patterns in periodically flooded Vojvodina soils, relevant to assessing whether one survey can support later sampling decisions.

sources.quote: The temporal stability of apparent electrical conductivity (ECa) spatial patterns was examined in a 62-hectare field subject to periodic flooding
transition zones require repeated measurement.

rationale.text: His project experience includes targeted coring, uncertainty maps and GIS deliverables for agricultural advisory users.

sources.quote: Field campaigns combined EM38 surveys, pXRF scanning, and targeted soil coring to obtain ECe, ESP, pH, texture, and organic carbon.
Regression-kriging was applied to generate 1:10 000-scale prediction maps and associated uncertainty surfaces.
Outputs were delivered to local agricultural extension services in open GIS formats.

rationale.text: He has delivered salinity and sodicity maps through paid commissions for agricultural cooperatives, providing relevant experience with commercial agronomic outputs.

sources.quote: Kosanović has carried out two paid soil survey commissions for agricultural cooperatives in Vojvodina, delivering ECe and ESP maps used for variable-rate gypsum application.

constraints.text: The operational design must resolve 0.3–0.8-hectare pockets without relying on blanket denser laboratory sampling; total fieldwork, laboratory costs and delivery time must fit the service economics.

we can't afford to sample more densely.

constraints.text: Historical data must be audited for usable salinity targets and comparable sampling and laboratory protocols before pooling ten years of observations; the stated routine outputs do not establish ECe or ESP coverage.

sources.quote: Imamo GPS koordinate svih dosadašnjih uzoraka i laboratorijske rezultate za oko 18.000 tačaka iz poslednjih deset godina.
Rezultati koje klijent vidi odnose se na pH, fosfor, kalijum, humus i potrebu za kalcifikacijom
Standardni agrohemijski protokoli po SRPS metodologiji za uzorkovanje i analizu

constraints.text: The workflow must provide zone guidance before dispatching the soil-sampling crew; any preliminary sensor survey must be explicitly scheduled and costed rather than assuming early-spring NDVI is sufficient.

salinitet ne vidi jasno na vegetacionim indeksima u ranom proleću.

constraints.text: A field-based pilot must secure instrument bookings and consumables funding. The researcher offers short-term site visits, but sustained project availability remains unconfirmed.

sources.quote: His EM38 and pXRF instruments are available to external partners subject to scheduling and consumables cost recovery.
Kosanović is available for short-term consultancy visits to company sites within Serbia.
He prefers collaborations that involve genuine field data collection rather than purely computational work.

constraints.text: Implementation must fit limited company development capacity and intermittent field support, with outputs compatible with the existing spatial database and portal.

risks: The published results do not validate detection of TloCare’s small Tisa floodplain pockets. Local spatial structure, soil conditions and survey timing may differ; the first experiment must test local calibration and pocket detection rather than importing published spacing or accuracy.
The closest sunflower study used both EM38 and pXRF. An EM38-only workflow is a transfer gap and should be compared with the combined-sensor approach before assuming equivalent performance.
ECa is a proxy rather than a direct salinity diagnosis. Texture and changing field conditions may alter its relationship with laboratory salinity and cause false alarms or missed pockets.
The historical archive may lack ECe, ESP, sampling-depth metadata or sufficiently recent reference observations. Its size alone does not establish suitability for salinity prediction.
A preliminary sensor pass, repeat surveys in unstable zones and adequate calibration sampling may erase laboratory savings. The affordable sample count and detection performance remain unproven.
Researcher availability for sustained supervision of the project, instrument dates, company budget, field access and delivery deadlines remain unknown.
A model dependent on newly collected dense sensor data may not meet the company's desired pre-dispatch workflow unless surveys can be reused or collected economically in advance.
questions: Which historical records contain ECe, ESP or other salinity measurements, and are sampling depth, date, laboratory method, parcel boundaries and quality-control metadata available?
Can the company provide the previously densely sampled Tisa parcels, including pocket boundaries and sunflower establishment observations, and secure access for new reference sampling?
What salinity threshold, minimum pocket-detection rate, tolerable false-alarm rate and spatial accuracy would make the service useful?
What are the current per-hectare fieldwork and laboratory costs, turnaround target, pilot budget and acceptable recurring cost ceiling?
Must predictions be available before any field visit, or is a separate advance EM38 survey acceptable? Can older sensor surveys be reused after local temporal-stability testing?
Can Kosanović confirm sustained joint-project availability, his role, instrument booking dates and cost-recovery terms?
Should the pilot compare EM38-only and EM38-plus-pXRF workflows, and who will fund the independent reference samples needed for spatially held-out validation?
Who will own and access the data and resulting models, and what GIS layers, uncertainty displays and sampling instructions must be delivered through the existing portal?
